xmldoc.short_description: Decode protobuf bytes to structs, columns, a table or a timetable.

syntax.syntax_item: [value, presence, report] = protobuf.decode(schema, type, bytes, name, value, ...)
[value, presence, report] = protobuf.decode(schema, type, bytes, 'Delimited', true, 'Layout', 'columns')

param_input_item.param_description: a schema from protobuf.load and a message type (full name or a unique trailing part).
a uint8 vector: encoded data, one message or a length-delimited stream with 'Delimited'.
logical (default false): the bytes are a stream of records, each one prefixed by its size as a varint.
'struct' (default, a 1xN struct array), 'columns' (a scalar struct of Nx1 columns with a presence output), 'table' or 'timetable'.
a field name or a list of names: only these are decoded. 'a.b' selects field b of the sub-message a at any depth.
control the mapping: Timestamp/Duration/wrappers as native values, enums as names, absent fields as their default, missing integers as NaN. See the protobuf page.
'skip' drops bad records (counted in report.Skipped), 'Workers' sets the decoding threads, 'KeepUnknown' keeps unknown fields in UnknownFields.

param_output_item.param_description: the decoded data in the requested layout.
columns layouts: a struct of Nx1 logical columns, true where a value is present, for fields that can be missing.
a struct with the fields Type, Records and Skipped.

description.p: protobuf.decode reads Protocol Buffers bytes back into Nelson values. A single message gives a struct; with 'Delimited', a stream gives a struct array, or columns, a table or a timetable with 'Layout'. Large streams are decoded on several threads.

The columns layouts return a presence output beside the data, so a value that is present but zero is told from one that is absent. Given back to protobuf.encode with 'Presence', the columns encode to the same bytes.
protobuf.read decodes straight from a file, a file identifier or a ZIP entry with the same options.

example_item.example_item_description: Decode a stream as columns with a presence output
